newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Austrian Airlines returns to Sarajevo.
newsitem.headline: Austrian Airlines returns to Sarajevo.

text.p: Austrian Airlines resumed flights to Sarajevo after a four-year break on Monday, the first non-Balkan commercial airline to return to the Bosnian capital's battle-scarred airport
An Austrian airlines Fokker 70 landed at 2:30 p.m. on Monday to inaugurate the service, which will operate on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday.
The only other foreign companies to fly to Sarajevo are Croatia airlines from from Zagreb and Slovenia's Adria Airlines via Zagreb.
Manfred Wiltner, director of Austrian Airlines' Bosnia office, said a larger aircraft with 111 seats would fly the Sarajevo-Vienna route for 686 German marks ($1,097) return, beginning April 7.
The company expected the flights to carry an average 50 percent capacity, Wiltner told Reuters.
"When we opened the route it was not for symbolic purposes. According to our research this route will be profitable," he said.
Wiltner said Austrian Airlines was hoping to deliver air cargo to Sarajevo as well but the city's airport still lacked storage space for commerical cargo.

In the meantime, the airline planned to offer cargo delivery for Sarajevo's large diplomatic community, he said. Austrian airline passenger planes flying to Sarajevo had up to five tons of cargo space, he said.
Some of the Bosnian war's worse fighting took place around the airport between the Sarajevo government and Serb separatists backed by the Yugoslav army.

United Nations peacekeeping soldiers operated the airport for humanitarian flights during most of the 1992-95 conflict. The NATO-led peace force which now polices the country's peace treaty runs a portion of the airport for military flights.
